stem: The following statements describe the term of “chimerism” after allogeneic HSCT. Select the CORRECT answer.

options.A: Although rare, some cases of hematological malignancies may have long-term survival despite persistent presence of mixed chimerism.
options.B: Mixed chimerism indicates the human body has 100% hematopoietic cells of donor origin within bone marrow, mixed with cells of recipient origin at other organs.
options.C: For patients of severe aplastic anemia receiving allogeneic HSCT, persistence of mixed chimerism usually indicates inevitable graft failure in the near future.
options.D: Chimerism can be readily determined using short tandem repeat (STR) test based on PCR method for a single locus of genomic DNA sequence.

ebmt_chapters: Ch21 Documentation of Engraftment and Chimerism After HCT (PDF p210–215)
Ch78 Acquired Bone Marrow Failure: Severe Aplastic Anemia and Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PDF p695–703)

stem: Select the CORRECT answer from following statements regarding monitoring minimal residual disease (MRD) after allogeneic HSCT

options.A: The use of PCR-based method to detect fusion genes can be applied to detect MRD in all the AML cases but not in patients of ALL.
options.B: The method of short tandem repeat (STR) used for determining the chimerism after allogeneic HSCT can sensitively detect the MRD in either AML or ALL.
options.C: In t(8;21) AML, the detection of RUNX1/RUNXITI transcripts may persist after allogeneic transplant without subsequent relapse.
options.D: In AML with chromosomal anomalies, conventional metaphase cytogenetics can detect residual leukemic cells with sensitivity equal to PCR method.

ebmt_chapters: Ch57 Monitoring Measurable Residual Disease in ALL and AML (PDF p516–524)
Ch21 Documentation of Engraftment and Chimerism After HCT (PDF p210–215)

stem: Select the CORRECT answer from the following statements describing use of donor lymphocyte infusion to treat the hematological malignancies relapsing after allo-HSCT.

options.A: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) can induce acute GVHD and marrow aplasia and carries a mortality rate around 5-10%.
options.B: The initial cell dose of DLI should be as large as possible to exert its GVL effect.
options.C: Repeated administration of DLI is prohibited in concern of the risk of severe GVHD.
options.D: DLI targets the malignant cells originating from recipient while sparing engrafted hematopoietic cells of donor origin, hence, severe cytopenia is rarely seen after the procedure.

ebmt_chapters: Ch59 Delayed Transfer of Immune Cells or the Art of Donor Lymphocyte Infusion (DLI) 2.0 (PDF p532–540)
Ch58 Prevention and Treatment of Relapse by Drugs (PDF p525–531)
